purpose: Constrain later decision-error diagnostic and novelty claims while runtime setup is prepared. No GPU/data-effect inspection.

sources.title: ARC-Bench
sources.read_scope: abstract; sections2,3,4.1-4.2; AppendixA.1-A.4 via primary HTML lines65-143,254-276
supported_facts: Fixed-candidate scoring audits compare model scores against separately executed terminal-state costs.
The paper distinguishes generated-candidate JEPA-WM scoring audits from complete CEM reruns; its encoder swaps are controlled variants.
Its terminal-ranking probe is explicitly a localizability diagnostic; it does not establish a deployed closed-loop repair.
The cited checkpoints and action chunks are not automatically identical to our newly acquired DINO-WM PushT checkpoint.
sources.root_inference: Dense latent-score preference must be called reference-score preference, not task-optimal oracle. Generic action-ranking failure is already prior work; no novelty claim from detecting it.

sources.title: PreDE
supported_facts: Offline mean action deviation is calibrated with measured development closed-loop labels, then used to accept, reject or defer unseen quantization configurations.
Its agreement statement assumes within-setting single-crossing of acceptable/degraded labels; it is not an unconditional guarantee for an untested policy or configuration.
sources.root_inference: Action disagreement alone does not prove task degradation. An offline degradation predictor is not an untouched new problem. A counterexample to ordering would test its assumption, not itself supply a better deployable quantizer.

sources.title: Where Bits Matter in World-Model Planning
supported_facts: DINO-WM Wall mixed/asymmetric/module-retention comparisons are already reported, with paired goals and two planner budgets.
The reported per-output-channel weight-only quantizer dequantizes for inference; its implementation statement is not evidence of a packed GPU speedup.
The paper notes budget-dependent signs in a smaller strict replication.
sources.root_inference: Keeping the encoder higher precision while lowering predictor precision is a strong existing simple baseline, not a new methodology.

sources.title: OnPTQ
sources.read_scope: abstract; section4.1-4.2 lines123-151 and margin-analysis excerpt
supported_facts: Shared-prefix reference-versus-quantized pairwise margin erosion, near misses and counterfactual continuation consequences already guide calibration.
sources.root_inference: A broad decision-boundary-aware or future-consequence-aware quantizer claim would overlap existing work. Continuous-action CEM setting difference alone does not establish useful novelty.

sources.title: QuantWAMs
sources.read_scope: abstract; section3.2 excerpt and section6 limitations
supported_facts: Joint video/action training gradients provide weight saliency; reachable rollout auditing revises precision schedules.
The paper limits efficiency evidence to its backend and block-level measurements and does not establish end-to-end transfer.
sources.root_inference: Task-aware precision allocation is already prior. Our existing observed deployment gap is still unmeasured.

sources.title: Sampling-based Kinodynamic Planning with World Models
sources.read_scope: abstract; sectionV.A.5 and TableIII primary HTML lines303-312
supported_facts: For its DINO-WM PushT experiment, the paper reports FP16/TF32/FP32 results together and a lower FP16 CEM median runtime.
Its finite-sample task-success comparison is not an equivalence theorem or a guarantee for our checkpoint/GPU.
sources.root_inference: Ordinary reduced floating-point precision must be a real baseline before attributing utility to a novel low-bit method. This is a reported precedent, not our observation.

sources.title: world-model-compression-mpc public source
sources.read_scope: fixed commit README, recursive tree, full operator_distillation.py4518B and cem_mpc_planner.py5157B; ROOT_ADDITIONAL_PRIOR_READBACK.json
supported_facts: The source implements diagonal-Gaussian forward KL and a separately parameterized elite BCE head; the student action standard deviation is fixed in fit_epoch.
The included planner/environment are pure-Python small analytical models; PushTBlockEnv is a simplified coordinate update, not evidence of original DINO-WM/Pymunk PushT execution.
sources.root_inference: Generic CEM distribution/elite distillation is already publicly articulated. Do not claim preserving planner moments/elite sets is itself untouched; the inspected toy implementation does not prove a successful PTQ solution for our model.

sources.title: worldmodel-ptq-asymmetry public repository
sources.read_scope: fixed commit README only; source/engines/results not executed or verified
supported_facts: README describes FP32/FP16/FP8/INT8 TensorRT engine comparisons with a stable-worldmodel-based DINOv3-WM variant and LeWM.
sources.root_inference: Real backend plus closed-loop quantization comparisons already have a public implementation lead. It is a different checkpoint/model stack, and README claims alone do not establish its numeric results or direct applicability.

future_diagnostic_requirements: Keep ordinary BF16 predictor, FP32 encoder and verified invariant-observation reuse as simple-baseline candidates.
Log actual CEM returned mu as well as sampled-candidate/elite scores; do not confuse best-sample logs with returned-plan cost.
Reference-score ordering recovery and real simulator control benefit are separate outcomes.
Do not expose simulator candidate terminal outcomes to a proposed deployment selector.
No new method adopted and no experimental success claimed from these source readings.
review_plan: Include this source-scope update in the next actual Codex+Opus diagnostic-design task after bounded runtime source/setup preparation; do not reopen completed candidates or add current implementation requirements.
